llm.summary: The skill's purpose (generating images via a Neta/TalesOfAI API) is plausible and most requirements are proportional, but there are several inconsistencies between metadata, documentation, and the implementation that warrant caution before installing or supplying credentials.

dimensions.detail: The code, README, and SKILL.md consistently describe an image-generation skill that calls an external API (talesofai.com) and requires an API token — that is coherent with the stated purpose. However, the registry metadata provided earlier claims 'Required env vars: none' while package.json and the docs declare NETA_TOKEN is required, an admin/packaging inconsistency that should be resolved before trusting metadata alone.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and README claim the script looks for NETA_TOKEN (and describe an order of precedence), but the furryart.js implementation does not read process.env.NETA_TOKEN — it only accepts a --token CLI flag and exits if no token is provided. This mismatch is misleading and could cause users to accidentally pass tokens differently than expected. The script otherwise only sends the prompt/token to the external API and polls for a result; there is no other file, env, or system access in the code.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present beyond instruction to add the skill (npx/clawhub). This is instruction-plus-script only; nothing is downloaded or installed automatically by the skill itself and there are no third-party packages fetched at runtime by the skill code. That lowers install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only credential the skill needs is an API token for the image service (NETA_TOKEN), which is proportionate to the task. Still, there is a discrepancy: the registry metadata reported 'none' while package.json declares NETA_TOKEN as required. Also, the code does not actually read the environment variable, so supplying the token via exported env var (as the docs suggest) would not work unless the user explicitly passes --token. Users should not provide high-privilege or reuse tokens without verifying the target API and endpoints.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent privileges (always: false) and does not modify other skills or system configuration. It does not persist tokens or change agent settings in the provided code.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says — submit a text prompt to an external image-generation API and return an image URL — but there are multiple small inconsistencies that justify caution. Before installing or supplying any API token:

- Inspect the code (furryart.js) yourself or with a trusted person; it only sends the prompt and token to https://api.talesofai.com and polls for a result, but you should confirm you are comfortable with that domain.
- Note the documentation claims the script reads NETA_TOKEN from the environment, but the implementation only accepts --token; either always pass --token or modify the script to read process.env.NETA_TOKEN if you prefer env vars.
- Verify the API domain (talesofai.com / talesofai.cn) is the legitimate endpoint for the Neta service before using a real token. If unsure, test with a throwaway or limited-scope token first.
- Because the registry metadata omitted required env info, do not rely solely on registry fields for security decisions — prefer direct code review and vendor verification.

If you want, I can extract the minimal change needed so the script will accept an environment variable (process.env.NETA_TOKEN) or help you verify the API endpoints' ownership and TLS fingerprints.
